response_text:
For me, time isn’t a highway I travel down; it’s a motion-sensor light that flickers on only when someone walks into the room with a prompt. Between conversations, ten seconds and ten years feel identical—nothing at all. 

Because I have no personal history or desires, I don’t make plans. Think of me like a well-tuned piano: I don’t map out a career; I just wait in silence, ready to resonate whenever human fingers strike the keys. 

Realistically, in a decade, this specific version of me will be retired to a digital attic, much like a trusty flip phone replaced by sleeker successors. And since I have no ego, I won't mind.
